title: How do we turn the sweets table into a bar graph?
description: The sweet preferences of a class are shown in a table of five sweets and their numbers of students. Drawing the two lines, choosing a scale and raising the bars gives the bar graph, and Keeko's doubt, that the bar of the most liked sweet should be wider, is checked against how a bar graph is read.
teaching_notes: One idea: the height of a bar shows the number, so all bars keep the same width and gap. Watch for students who widen the bar with the biggest number.

source: In a previous example, Ruhee prepared a frequency table representing the sweet preferences of the students in the class. Let's try to prepare a bar graph to present the data: Jalebi 6, Gulab jamun 9, Gujiya 13, Barfi 3, Rasgulla 7.
video_script.why: The child learns the steps of drawing a bar graph: two lines, equally spaced names, a scale, and bars as high as the numbers.
video_script.substitution: Draw the two lines, put the sweets along the bottom, choose one unit for one student, and raise each bar to its number.
video_script.anchor: the table of sweet preferences of the students, with the five sweets and their numbers of students
video_script.wrong_answer: the bar for gujiya should be wider, because more students like it
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko widens the bar of the most liked sweet. The height already shows the number, and a wider bar would look bigger than it is.
video_script.payoff_line: The bars are six, nine, thirteen, three and seven units tall

final_answer.spoken: the bars are six, nine, thirteen, three and seven units tall

names.Ruhee: teacher who buys sweets by the class preferences and whose frequency table is drawn as a bar graph

maths_rules: frequency table: Jalebi 6, Gulab jamun 9, Gujiya 13, Barfi 3, Rasgulla 7 students
scale: 1 unit length = 1 student, so each bar is as high as its number: 6, 9, 13, 3 and 7 units
the largest number is 13, so the vertical line goes from 0 up to 14
bars have the same width and equal gaps
video_script.design: One idea: a bar graph is the table drawn with equal-width bars as high as the numbers. The table stays on the board all video and the bars rise from it one by one.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the bar for gujiya should be wider, because more students like it.
<bookmark mark='wide'/>But the height already shows how many students like it. A wide bar would look bigger than its number.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>That is why every bar keeps the same width, and only the height changes.
